title: Bounded above acyclic complexes compute a left derived functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and assume $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives: every object admits an epimorphism from an object $P$ for which every map $P\to Y$ lifts across every epimorphism $X\to Y$. Every bounded above cochain complex $X$ has a quasi-isomorphism $P\to X$ with $P$ bounded above and each $P^i$ projective; when $X^i=0$ for $i>b$, one can require $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and right exact (it preserves cokernels and finite direct sums), and suppose its total left derived functor $LV:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists, i.e. in Situation 05S8 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with the homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$, its quasi-isomorphisms and the functor $Q\circ V$, the left derived functor is defined at every object, with canonical comparison $\varepsilon_C:LV(QC)\to Q(V(C))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every bounded above complex of projective objects $P$, $\varepsilon_P$ is an isomorphism. Call an object $A$ left $V$-acyclic when $\varepsilon_{A[0]}:LV(A[0])\to V(A)[0]$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded above complex $C$ of left $V$-acyclic objects, $\varepsilon_C$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, if $a:C\to X$ is a quasi-isomorphism with such $C$, the canonical identification of $LV(QX)$ with $Q(V(C))$ is $\varepsilon_C\circ LV(Qa)^{-1}$. These identifications are natural for maps between augmented resolutions: a square $a'f=ha$ gives $Q(V(f))\varepsilon_C LV(Qa)^{-1}=\varepsilon_{C'}LV(Qa')^{-1}LV(Qh)$.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist; Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, applied to bounded above projectives; dual of Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity. The last equality is naturality of the canonical comparison. Defined at every object: Definition Tag 05S9.

proof.text: Fix $b$ with $X^i=0$ for $i>b$. Construct $a:P\to X$ by downward recursion, with $P^i=0$ above $b$. The induction invariant is that $Z^{n+1}(P)\to Z^{n+1}(X)$ is epic, where $Z^i=\ker d^i$; above $b$ this is the identity of zero. Form the compatible-pair object $T^n=X^n\times_{Z^{n+1}(X)} Z^{n+1}(P)$, using the corestriction of $d_X^n$ and the cycle map induced by $a$. Choose a projective epimorphism $P^n\twoheadrightarrow T^n$ by enough projectives. Its two components define $a^n$ and $d_P^n$, the latter followed by $Z^{n+1}(P)\hookrightarrow P^{n+1}$. Thus $d_P^{n+1}d_P^n=0$ and $a^{n+1}d_P^n=d_X^na^n$. To check $a^n$ is epic, refine an arbitrary generalized element $x$ of $X^n$ to lift $d_Xx$ through the epic cycle map, then refine again through $P^n\twoheadrightarrow T^n$. The refinement criterion (a) proves the assertion. If $x$ is a cycle, lift the pair $(x,0)$ instead; its lifts are cycles, so the same criterion proves $Z^n(P)\to Z^n(X)$ epic and closes the induction. This constructs all degrees, indexed by $b-n\in\mathbf N$, without a limit operation.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist (3), explicit dual recursive construction; epimorphic refinements as in Homology Tag 05PK. Only the refinement criterion stated by the cited node is used.

proof.text: The epic cycle maps from Step 1 imply that $H^n(a)$ is epic. For injectivity, take a generalized cycle $p:T\to P^n$ whose image class in $H^n(X)$ is zero. By the cokernel refinement criterion (c), after an epimorphic refinement there is $x:T'\to X^{n-1}$ with $a^np=d_X^{n-1}x$. Then $(x,p)$ is a generalized element of $T^{n-1}$, since $p$ is a cycle. Lift it after a further epimorphic refinement through $P^{n-1}\twoheadrightarrow T^{n-1}$. Its lift $r$ satisfies $d_P^{n-1}r=p$. Hence the class of $p$ is zero. Generalized elements of $H^n(P)$ themselves lift after refinement through $Z^n(P)\twoheadrightarrow H^n(P)$, so this proves the kernel of $H^n(a)$ is zero by criteria (a)--(c). Therefore $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. All terms are projective and the specified upper bound is retained, proving the first clause.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist (3), verification of the recursive resolution using generalized elements.

proof.text: Let $P$ be any bounded above complex of projectives. It is K-projective by the cited bounded-above criterion: its Hom complex into every acyclic $N$ is acyclic. Degree-zero cocycles of that complex are the chain maps $P\to N$ and degree-zero coboundaries are the maps $d_Nh+hd_P$, so every chain map $P\to N$ is null-homotopic, which is the K-projectivity of the cited Hom bijection. For every quasi-isomorphism $s:Y\to P$ in $K(\mathcal A)$, the cited Hom bijection lifts $Q(s)^{-1}$ uniquely to $t_s:P\to Y$ in $K(\mathcal A)$. Its injectivity gives $s t_s=1_P$. It also gives $u t_s=t_{s'}$ whenever $s'u=s$, because the two maps have the same image under $Q$. Thus $1_P$ is an initial object of the denominator category $S/P$, with unique arrows $t_s:1_P\to s$. Put $F=Q\circ V$ on the homotopy category. The maps $F(t_s):F(P)\to F(Y)$ form a cone on the denominator diagram. In the definition of essentially constant pro-diagram, choose stage $j_0=1_P$, retraction $r=1_{F(P)}$, and common stage $k=1_P$ for every $s$. The factorization condition is then the identity $F(t_s)=F(t_s)$. This diagram therefore has essential value $F(P)$, and its canonical map to its stage $1_P$ is an isomorphism. By the assumed meaning of $LV$ in Situation 05S8 and Definition 05S9 this map is $\varepsilon_P$. This proves projective-complex computation directly, including projective objects placed in degree zero and the zero object.

source.place: Tags 05S8 and 05S9, denominator-diagram definition; dual of the denominator-section argument in lemma-injective-acyclic. The two K-projective facts are the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal E$ denote the class of left $V$-acyclic objects. By Step 3 it contains all projectives and zero. Applied to the split short exact sequence $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$, clause (1) of the cited short-exact-sequence lemma shows that $\mathcal E$ is closed under finite direct sums. Clause (2) says that for an epimorphism between objects of $\mathcal E$ its kernel again belongs to $\mathcal E$, and applying $V$ to that short exact sequence remains short exact. The lemma applies because $V$ is additive and right exact, $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives, and its everywhere-defined total left derived comparison is exactly the one assumed in the item.

source.place: Dual of Tag 015D, lemma-F-acyclic-ses, clauses (1) and (2).

proof.text: Now let $C$ be bounded above and termwise in $\mathcal E$, and choose $a:P\to C$ by Steps 1--2. Its mapping cone $E=\operatorname{Cone}(a)$ is acyclic by the cited cone criterion and has terms $E^n=C^n\oplus P^{n+1}\in\mathcal E$ by Steps 3--4. Choose $b$ above which $E$ vanishes. Descend from $Z^{b+1}(E)=0\in\mathcal E$. Acyclicity gives short exact sequences $0\to Z^n(E)\to E^n\to Z^{n+1}(E)\to0$. At each stage clause (2) of the short-exact-sequence lemma, with middle term $E^n$ and quotient $Z^{n+1}(E)$, puts $Z^n(E)$ in $\mathcal E$ and makes the image sequence under $V$ short exact. Since $d_{V(E)}^n$ factors as the epic map $V(E^n)\to V(Z^{n+1}(E))$ followed by its monic inclusion in $V(E^{n+1})$, these sequences give $\operatorname{im}d_{V(E)}^{n-1}=V(Z^n(E))=\ker d_{V(E)}^n$ in every degree. Thus $V(E)$ is acyclic. The cone formula uses only a finite direct sum, additive maps and a minus sign, so additivity identifies $V(E)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(V(a))$. The cone criterion now shows $V(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity, dual conclusion; explicit descending-cycle proof from dual Tag 015D. The cone formula is the one in the cited derived-category definition.

proof.text: Naturality of the given canonical comparison at $a:P\to C$ gives $Q(V(a))\,\varepsilon_P=\varepsilon_C\,LV(Qa)$. Step 3 makes $\varepsilon_P$ invertible, Step 5 makes $Q(V(a))$ invertible, and $Qa$ is invertible because $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Solving gives $\varepsilon_C=Q(V(a))\varepsilon_P LV(Qa)^{-1}$, so $\varepsilon_C$ is an isomorphism. For any quasi-isomorphism $c:C\to X$ with bounded above termwise acyclic $C$, this gives the required canonical identification $I_c=\varepsilon_C LV(Qc)^{-1}$. This construction uses only the specified comparison and localization, so it does not depend on the auxiliary projective resolution.

source.place: Tag 015E, canonical comparison; formal naturality and inversion in the localized category.

proof.text: For the square $a'f=ha$ of the statement, naturality gives $Q(V(f))\varepsilon_C=\varepsilon_{C'}LV(Qf)$, and functoriality gives $LV(Qa')LV(Qf)=LV(Qh)LV(Qa)$. Multiplying the latter equality by the two inverses yields $LV(Qf)LV(Qa)^{-1}=LV(Qa')^{-1}LV(Qh)$. Substitution in the former equality proves $Q(V(f))\varepsilon_C LV(Qa)^{-1}=\varepsilon_{C'}LV(Qa')^{-1}LV(Qh)$, exactly the claimed naturality equation.
